title: COMP 4537 · Lecture 6
subtitle: Promises: idempotent PUT vs POST vs PATCH, callbacks, the three states, the executor, the event-loop order of Examples 1 to 12, chaining with then, catch and finally, async and await
description: Lecture 6 of Amir Amintabar's course: a review of HTTP verbs (PUT replaces, PATCH updates a property, PUT is idempotent and POST is not), first-class functions and callbacks, why a function doing asynchronous work needs both a value and an outcome, then the JavaScript Promise: the boss-and-raise analogy, pending, fulfilled and rejected (fulfilled and rejected are settled), the annotated constructor with its five notes, the executor running immediately, settle-once, Promise.resolve, and the deck's Examples 1 to 12 with their log orders (synchronous code, then microtasks, then timers). Then chaining (returning a value fulfils the next promise, throwing rejects it), .catch as .then(null, f), .finally, unhandled rejections, the DevTools views of a promise before and after 5 seconds, async and await, two successive AJAX calls and callback hell, GET vs POST response size and the corrected readyState table. Event-loop and promise-chain playbacks for every example; twelve new output-order programs; a 30-item mock quiz.
intro:
:::quiz Midterm weight
The midterm is 30 % of the course and covers lectures 1 to 6 in full plus the Node-to-MySQL part of lecture 7. By slide count this lecture is about an eighth of that scope, but the exam's coding questions ask you to write the console output of short programs with timers and promises, and that skill is taught here: expect this lecture to carry more than its share. Quizzes 8 and 9 were both on it. Closed book except one letter-sized sheet, both sides: the ordering rule, the three states and the chaining rules belong on it.
:::
